title: CoPHo: Classifier-guided Conditional Topology Generation with Persistent Homology

problem.claim: Topology data are often scarce, creating a need to generate synthetic graphs with desired properties.

gap.claim: Existing diffusion approaches either require retraining for each attribute or fail to account for topology scale and practical constraints.

contributions.claim: The paper incorporates gradients from a pre-trained graph-level classifier into the discrete reverse diffusion posterior to steer graph generation toward specified structural properties.
CoPHo builds a persistent homology filtration over intermediate graphs and uses its features as guidance signals during denoising.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four generic/network datasets reportedly show that CoPHo outperforms existing methods at matching target metrics.
The authors further report transferability validation on the QM9 molecular dataset.
Code is reported as available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scarce topology data motivate synthetic graph generation with desired properties.
Prior diffusion methods have retraining, real-time, topology-scale, and practical-constraint limitations.
A pre-trained graph-level classifier guides the discrete reverse diffusion posterior.
CoPHo uses persistent homology features from intermediate graphs to guide denoising.
The authors report results on four generic/network datasets and transferability validation on QM9.

source_observation.claim: Classifier guidance is incorporated into the discrete reverse diffusion posterior to target structural properties.

interpretation.claim: A pre-trained classifier may provide reusable conditional control without retraining the diffusion model for every attribute.

application.claim: For constrained graph generation, consider separating conditional guidance from the base diffusion model when the guidance signal is available.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance across all attributes, scales, or practical deployment settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four generic/network datasets.
Quantitative target metrics, baselines, and result magnitudes are omitted.
Training details, computational costs, and real-time performance are unspecified.
The scope and results of transferability on QM9 are unspecified.
